nodes.description: De novo heterozygous variants confined to the N-terminal DNA-binding zinc fingers 2 and 3 of HELIOS: an in-frame tandem duplication of exon 5 (p.Gly136_Ser191dup) and a missense change at a base-recognition residue of zinc finger 2 (p.Gly153Arg). The variant proteins are expressed and interfere with wild-type HELIOS in a dominant negative manner, which the authors propose explains a more profound, syndromic phenotype than that of loss-of-function IKZF2 alleles.

evidence.snippet: We performed detailed phenotypic, genomic and functional investigations on two unrelated individuals with a phenotype of immune dysregulation combined with syndromic features including craniofacial differences, sensorineural hearing loss and congenital abnormalities.

nodes.description: In mice, Helios is expressed in postnatal cochlear outer hair cells and is required for their functional maturation (prestin-dependent electromotility); an Ikzf2 point mutant (cello) has early-onset sensorineural hearing loss. Imaging of both ICHAD probands showed structurally normal inner ears, consistent with a hair-cell rather than a structural cause, but no human cochlear tissue has been examined.

nodes.description: Patient CD4+ T cells are hyperactive, secrete elevated levels of nearly all T helper cytokines and proliferate readily; CD8+ T cells show increased activation; and regulatory T cells develop in normal numbers but aberrantly produce T helper cytokines. This loss of immune restraint is the proposed basis of the autoimmune and atopic features. It rests on one patient's cells.
